[3730] South African Military Health Service

[3731] The SA Military Health Service will prepare, provide and deploy military health capabilities to support the landward and maritime defence strategies, inclusive of the air defence and Special Forces components thereof

[3732] The SA Military Health Service must be able to conduct and sustain layered military health support to protracted operations over long distances

[3733] Such layered health services will ensure both force health protection and force health sustainment

[3734] The SA Military Health Service capability sets will include: a. Command and Control

[3735] A medical command and control capability is required for the effective conduct of medical operations

[3736] These are provided through static and mobile capabilities

[3737] The operational command and control capability will reside in the Medical Command, whereas the brigades and battalion groups will provide tactical command and control

[3738] b. Health Intelligence Capability

[3739] A health intelligence capability, including targeted epidemiology, will provide tactical health intelligence to determine and coordinate the health support plan

[3740] The summated tactical intelligence picture will be fed up the operations staff line to the operational and strategic levels

[3741] c. Deployable Military Health Support Capability

[3742] The medical brigades and their deployable components are required to render support to division-strength combat forces

[3743] Depending on the nature, size and duration of an operation, sub-elements of the medical brigade may be mobilised and deployed to support operations

[3744] These sub-elements are: Medical battalion groups to support brigade-strength combat forces with inherent capabilities to sustain task group functions

[3745] Medical task groups to support battalion-strength combat forces and may be specialised in specific areas of operational support, such as airborne forces, maritime components or Special Forces

[3746] Medical task teams will support company-strength combat forces

[3747] The following specialist capabilities may be embedded in the medical task groups and medical teams

[3748] Emergency Care Capability

[3749] Operational emergency care providing battlefield resuscitation, basic evacuation of casualties and first-line primary health care for treatment of minor ailments

[3750] Specifically equipped evacuation teams manage the evacuation of casualties on land and by air and assist in maritime evacuations

[3751] Environmental Health Capability

[3752] A deployable environmental health capability is required to support deployed forces with environmental health aspects

[3753] Chemical, Biological and Radiological (CBR) Defence Capability

[3754] CBR defence capability to detect chemical, biological and radiation threats and to further treat contaminated personnel, casualties and vehicles

[3755] Oral Health Care

[3756] A deployable oral health care capability that provides operational care consisting of emergency and essential dental care

[3757] The capability renders support during operations for canine patrols and explosive detection

[3758] Animal health capabilities are also deployed in support of search-and-rescue operations to take care of search dogs

[3759] The deployable military health support capability must be able to provide the following levels of clinical care in a peace support operation

[3760] Level 1 Medical Post

[3761] This provides a lifesaving capability, stabilisation, primary and secondary health care and evacuation to the next level

[3762] A level 1 medical post consists of resuscitation, surgical and minor ailment treatment capabilities

[3763] Level 2 Field Hospital

[3764] This capability provides triage, emergency resuscitation and stabilisation, surgery, second-line health care, general specialist services (general surgery, anaesthesia, and orthopaedic surgery and specialist internal medicine services), pharmacy, basic laboratory facilities, basic diagnostic capabilities, dental care, operational stress management, social work interventions, casualty evacuation to the next level and a preventative health service

[3765] Static Military Health Support Capability

[3766] The static military health support capability will render health sustainment to forces while at base, their families and other eligible persons

[3767] This service is delivered through base-orientated infrastructure

[3768] i. Sickbays and Military Medical Clinics

[3769] Sickbays and military medical clinics are positioned within geographical concentrations of designated beneficiaries and render a primary health care service through various components of the multi-professional health team

[3770] These facilities are normally positioned within unit lines

[3771] Palliative care is delivered through community-orientated home-based care, supported by hospice capabilities

[3772] iii. Military Base Hospitals

[3773] The military base hospital facilities provide a comprehensive primary and secondary health care capability in larger military bases with an admission and operating theatre capability

[3774] These can be configured as level 2 hospitals in peace support operations

[3775] Level 2 hospitals are generally established at existing infrastructure, and include specialist diagnostic resources, specialist surgical and medical capabilities, ancillary health services, dentistry, psychology and social work

[3776] iv. Military Hospitals

[3777] The military hospital facilities are positioned in specific geographical locations, based on the military footprint, to render a comprehensive hospitalisation service to patients

[3778] These capabilities are also utilised in support of operations

[3779] Military hospitals render secondary and tertiary levels of care including rehabilitation functions

[3780] These can be configured for level 4 hospitals in peace support operations and normally comprise specialist surgical and medical procedures, reconstruction, rehabilitation, convalescence, and psychological and social support

[3781] Specialised Institutes

[3782] Specialised institutes render a specialist function in specific areas of military medicine through specialised capabilities and research

[3783] MILITARY HEALTH FORCE DESIGN

[3784] The Military Health Service provides combat service support

[3785] This is done through force health protection of deployed elements of the combat services and force health sustainment of non-deployed military personnel and their dependants, military veterans and their dependants and other designated persons

[3786] The Force Design of the SA Military Health Service must therefore be such that it can meet these responsibilities

[3787] To this end capabilities are grouped under a Medical Command and organised into a level 4 base hospital, and three military health brigades, each with a level 3 specialist hospital, each with battalion groups under command

[3788] The battalion groups will consist of both static and deployable elements, these being medical task groups, level 2 static medical facilities inclusive of sick bays and/or deployable level 2 field hospitals

[3789] The three military health brigades will be aligned and organised to support the mechanised division, motorised division and contingency brigade of the SA Army respectively

[3790] The military health brigade supporting the contingency brigade will also support the SA Air Force and the SA Navy

[3791] The military health brigade headquarters assigned to support the army divisions are to be geographically co-located with these divisional headquarters

[3792] The medical task groups of the medical battalion groups are to be assigned to the combat formations they support

[3793] MILITARY HEALTH MIGRATION PRIORITIES

[3794] In migrating towards the future SA Military Health Service Force Design: a. Priority emphasis must be given to the establishment of the medical brigades and their subordinate structures

[3795] b. Consideration is to be given to establishing a dedicated SA Military Health Service military police element to have “own” military police capability under command during operations

[3796] SOUTH AFRICAN SPECIAL FORCES SA SPECIAL FORCES CAPABILITY

[3797] The SA Special Forces shall be organised as a Special Forces Command under command of the Chief of the Defence Force, operating in support of the landward and maritime defence strategies, and for the conducting of specific Special Force operations

[3798] South Africa’s increasingly complex and unstable security environment dictates an increasing reliance on SA Special Forces in defence operations, indicating an expansion of the current Special Forces capability in the landward, airborne and amphibious operational domains

[3799] SA Special Forces will be competent in the physical, informational and psychological dimensions of warfare

[3800] The SA Special Forces must be balanced, technologically advanced and able to conduct and sustain protracted operations over long distances and across the spectrum of conflict

[3801] The SA Special Forces capabilities must be suited to: strategic reconnaissance; ordered strategic tasks; deep reconnaissance and other tasks in support of the combat services; and the execution of SA Special Forces operations including hostage rescue, urban and anti-terror operations

[3802] The SA Special Forces shall be employed as an enabler throughout the spectrum of operations, requiring the maintenance of a small but permanently ready force for the conduct of joint or autonomous military operations, or in collaboration with Police Service task forces and other Special Forces capabilities within the region

[3803] Special Forces intelligence will provide tactical intelligence regarding the opposing force, terrain, population and other factors that influence detailed tactical planning and the successful execution of operations

[3804] The summated tactical intelligence picture will be fed up the operations staff line to the operational and strategic levels

[3805] The Special Forces Command will not be structured with their own inherent air, naval and support assets

[3806] Services and Divisions have a distinct responsibility towards ensuring the strategic capability of Special Forces through participation in Special Forces training and employment, as well as identified specialist elements to render Special Forces support

[3807] Personnel and equipment provided in support of such training and operations must meet the rigorous criteria demanded in this specialist environment

[3808] The following, inter alia, will be established in the Special Forces Command to meet the operational requirements of the Defence Force: a. Command and control capability

[3809] b. Triphibious capability (airborne, amphibious, urban and anti-terror combat capability

[3810] c. Special Forces training capability

[3811] d. Special Forces support capability

[3812] Related defence acquisitions pursued by other Services and Divisions should be supportive of Special Forces requirements

[3813] Included are heavy and medium fixed-wing lift and air supply, heavy rotary-wing lift and interoperability with naval assets

[3814] The SA Special Forces have a responsibility to support the SA Army in establishing its contingency (special operations) capability

[3815] SPECIAL FORCES ‘FORCE DESIGN’

[3816] The SA Special Forces will consist of operational regiments that will specialise in airborne and amphibious strategic reconnaissance as well as urban and anti-terror operations

[3817] The SA Special Forces will have responsibility for strategic reconnaissance and other strategic tasks, for deep reconnaissance in support of the combat services and for the execution of certain special operations, amongst others hostage rescue outside South Africa

[3818] Figure 10-5 below demonstrates the required Special Forces capabilities

[3819] Figure 10-5: Special Forces Capabilities SPECIAL FORCES MIGRATION PRIORITIES In migrating to the future Special Forces force design, priority emphasis (Milestone 2) must be placed on increasing the capacity of the existing regiments by one Special Forces commando each (including resources, infrastructure, housing, etc) to be able to deal with the diversity of tasks emanating from the Defence Environmental Analysis and Defence Intelligence Estimate

[3820] In the medium term (Milestone 3) it will entail the establishment of an additional Special Forces regiment

[3821] Given the sensitive nature of some of the tasks, the organisation must have an inherent capacity to protect itself in high-risk environments

[3822] A unique approach to recruitment, training, termination of service and leadership development is required to ensure that Special Forces personnel are effectively managed

[3823] Conditions of service need to reflect these unique requirements

[3824] Personnel need to conform to the highest level of security clearance

[3825] INFORMATION WARFARE

[3826] The Defence Force is to take the lead in providing for common defence against an attack intended to disrupt or disable South Africa’s key national information systems and infrastructure

[3827] To this end the Defence Force will develop comprehensive defensive Information Warfare capabilities, which will be tied into the intelligence-related information systems of the intelligence services

[3828] The Defence Information Warfare Capability focuses on six areas, namely: Network Warfare; Electronic Warfare; Psychological Operations; Information-Based Warfare; Information Infrastructure Warfare; and Command and Control Warfare

[3829] The focus areas are defined as follows: a. Network Warfare (Netwar): To exploit or use the information systems (offensive) of an adversary and to protect all defence information systems (defensive) to ensure use for own forces

[3830] b. Electronic Warfare: To exploit or use electromagnetic energy to determine, exploit, reduce or prevent hostile use of the electromagnetic spectrum while retaining its friendly use

[3831] c. Psychological Operations: To conduct planned psychological activities in peace, conflict and war in order to create attitudes and behaviour favourable to the achievement of political and military objectives

[3832] These operations include psychological action and warfare activities designed to achieve the desired psychological effect

[3833] d. Information-Based Warfare: To enhance situational awareness at the operational and tactical levels as well as to degrade that of an adversary

[3834] e. Information Infrastructure Warfare: To protect own information infrastructure and to attack or exploit an adversary’s information infrastructure

[3835] f. Command and Control Warfare: To conduct Information Warfare on the battlefield by causing a disjuncture between an adversary’s command structure and its commanded forces

[3836] DEFENCE BALANCING PRINCIPLES Defence planning is both a science and an art

[3837] It requires decisions that will affect the defence of the country for decades, and that involve considerable investment of human, industrial and financial capital; and those decisions must be based on the evolving strategic situation, or what threats might arise

[3838] There is thus always a real risk that the most carefully considered assessment could be entirely overturned within a short time by unforeseeable events, such as intervention by an external major power

[3839] It is neither possible nor affordable to prepare for every eventuality

[3840] The only practical approach to defence planning is to maintain balanced capabilities that: a. Enable the country to meet existing challenges effectively; b

[3841] Enable the country to deal effectively with foreseeable contingencies; c. Are flexible and can meet developing challenges or threats; and that d

[3842] Provide the foundation on which to build stronger forces when required, within a timeframe that is realistic relative to the strategic situation

[3843] The balanced set of capabilities must be continuously evaluated against the evolving strategic situation, and refocused, adapted or expanded as the situation dictates

[3844] There are ten key areas in which balance must be maintained: a. Among the combat services and the supporting services and staff divisions

[3845] There is a clear need to have the right balance among ground, naval and air force elements, and to have optimal balance between ‘teeth’ and ‘tail’

[3846] There is often pressure to improve the ratio of 'teeth' to 'tail', which is logical but which also holds the risk of developing forces that cannot sustain operations

[3847] Between Regulars and Reserves

[3848] A balance of Regulars and Reserves - Regulars to provide the core and deal with crises, and the Reserves to augment and expand the force when necessary

[3849] Between forces for local and expeditionary operations

[3850] Any country must in the first instance look to its own defence, but some countries must also, in their own interests, look to regional security and stability

[3851] South Africa must be able to undertake expeditionary operations, be they constabulary or peace support in nature

[3852] d. Between ‘high tech’ and ‘low tech’

[3853] ‘High tech’ is tempting, can give a very real edge over opponents and can be the most cost-effective option

[3854] But ‘high tech’ can also be costly to achieve and maintain

[3855] Low tech" is tempting because it is in most cases cheaper, but can prove to be a false economy if the opposing forces are better equipped

[3856] Technology decisions must be taken judiciously on a case-by-case basis

[3857] e. Between local and foreign equipment

[3858] Local will give strategic independence, provide equipment optimized for the theatre and for the Defence Force’s operational style, and can have valuable spin-offs for the wider economy

[3859] Local manufacture under licence can also be an option

[3860] Key items that will be manufactured locally include munitions, batteries and spares, secure command and control communications, Information Warfare equipment and other equipment required in large quantities

[3861] Complex equipment that is needed in small quantities is generally optimally acquired military-off-the-shelf

[3862] A much larger sourcing of materiel from local suppliers could serve as an impetus to re-industrialisation

[3863] f. Between current equipment and future technology

[3864] The Defence Force must acquire the equipment it requires to conduct current operations and to meet potential short-notice challenges

[3865] But equipment acquisition will be phased to avoid the problem of block obsolescence facing the Defence Force at a critical time

[3866] Under-equipping and over-equipping can be equally dangerous

[3867] While sufficient consideration must be given to research and development, care must be taken to not over-specify requirements in a race of technology, thereby detracting from the general principle of acquiring equipment military-off-the-shelf

[3868] g. Between preparation for a ‘short’ war or a ‘long’ war

[3869] South Africa will ensure adequate reserves of equipment and support for more protracted operations by ensuring the availability of strategic stocks

[3870] Between preparation for ‘high intensity’ and ‘low intensity’ operations

[3871] Armies are often accused of planning for ‘the last war’ and not for ‘the war to come’

[3872] South Africa will address this challenge by being prepared for a balance of high intensity and low intensity operations

[3873] In preparation for probable, possible and 'impossible' threats

[3874] Assuming a particular threat to be ‘impossible’ is irresponsibly dangerous

[3875] All contingencies will be identified and then prioritised by assessing the risk thereof; being a function of the probability of occurrence and the level of impact should that occurrence occur

[3876] j. Between defence expenditure and other government expenditure

[3877] An under-funded Defence Force will be disjointed and unable to meet its constitutional obligations

[3878] South Africa will endeavour to find the balance between spending on development and social programmes and national security imperatives

[3879] THE MILITARY EDUCATION, TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT IMPERATIVE Leadership lies at the centre of organisational excellence

[3880] The importance of exemplary military leadership cannot be overemphasised as any failure of the Defence Force in the execution of its mandate has dire and disastrous consequences for the state

[3881] It is for this reason that the Defence Force cannot compromise on the education, training and development of its leaders

[3882] Military leadership is rooted in the burden of command and there can be no compromise in the development of confident and competent men and women who will be placed in positions of authority

[3883] Throughout human history, military action has been shaped by the character and competence of those in command

[3884] Leadership is an intangible quality and, ultimately, the effect of the integration of a number of traits within individuals centred on the “what” the leader should be, know and do

[3885] Dynamic, visionary and transformational leadership, underpinned with knowledge, skill and attitude, is the foundation for future successful leaders in the Defence Force

[3886] To this end, defence leaders will be subject to intensive education, training and development programmes

[3887] Education, training and development, coupled to the exposure to military complexity over defined periods of time, is the proven pathway for the development of military leaders with the required character, knowledge, skills and attitudes

[3888] Military professionalism, based upon core military values, ethics and a robust professional ethos, is the foundation for the future military leader

[3889] Throughout the world, militaries are recognised as key institutions for the development of leadership within societies

[3890] The leadership foundation inculcated in the young men and women of both the Regular and Reserve components of the military will thus profoundly influence society as a whole

[3891] The Defence Force, through its leadership development programmes and the highly trained and disciplined members it cultivates, contributes significantly to the development of South Africa’s youth and society as a whole

[3892] The military professional education, training and development of young men and women will thus make a direct and significant contribution to national development and the future success of South Africa

[3893] The principles contained in this chapter apply equally to members of both the Regulars and Reserves

[3894] It is recognised however that because of the part-time nature of the service of the Reserves and their commitment to their civilian careers, flexibility will be required in the implementation of the principles

[3895] REQUIREMENT Defence requires an education, training and development programme, linked to a doctrine regime, to mould its members into informed, competent and cohesive military professionals for institutional and operational excellence across the spectrum of conflict

[3896] The guiding principle is that all programmes and courses will require formal assessment and examination for certification and graduation

[3897] GUIDING DEFENCE PRINCIPLES Ensuring that the Defence Force will strive to be seen as a representative and trusted non-partisan national asset, the following overarching defence principles are applied to the education, training and development of its members: a

[3898] The Defence Force is subject to sound civil control and oversight through the Commander-in-Chief, the Executive and the Legislature

[3899] The Defence Force is compliant with national law and regulations and international law (specifically international humanitarian law

[3900] Due consideration and cognisance are given to the unique nature of the Defence Force relative to the wider public service

[3901] The Defence Force is an agile, balanced, flexible and technologically advanced force supported by appropriate science, engineering and technology capabilities

[3902] The Defence Force is to cultivate and maintain a high standard of military professionalism

[3903] Soldiers are skilled, healthy, fit, and highly disciplined professionals imbued with a high level of morale, sense of duty and pride in themselves, their capabilities and their equipment

[3904] Soldiers are led by exemplary, competent, ethical and dynamic leaders

[3905] Mission command is the foundation of the defence leadership philosophy

[3906] The Defence Force is broadly representative of the people of South Africa, with due consideration being given to matters of equity, including gender and otherwise-abled persons

[3907] EDUCATION, TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT PRINCIPLES

[3908] The following principles are pursued to enhance defence education, training and development: a. Notwithstanding the broader development of its members, defence education, training and development has a primary focus on the defence mandate, the development of a warrior ethos and the ability to execute successful combat operations

[3911] c. Development of defence members is a line function and therefore a command responsibility throughout all levels of Defence

[3914] f. Defence presents accredited learning programmes that satisfy its organisational objectives as well as its human capital requirements

[3915] g. Education, training and development opportunities support individual career plans and individual learning pathways

[3916] h. Education, training and development is delivered effectively through tailored infrastructure and sufficient capacity, and coupled to appropriate methodologies and delivery systems, such as blended-learning and e-learning

[3917] i. Individual members take co-responsibility with the defence organisation for their own continuous professional education and actively seek access to education, training and development opportunities

[3918] The development of defence personnel is measured by the value that development initiatives have added to individual competence in the workplace and by their contribution to the success of military operations

[3919] k. Distance and e-learning will be emphasised to enable more Reserve members to avail themselves of the opportunity for empowerment and development

[3921] The defence leadership development programmes provide sufficient capacity to both ensure the requirements of the Defence Force and make a significant contribution to public sector and private sector leadership through its Reserves

[3936] Education is an open knowledge-driven process

PROFESSIONAL MILITARY EDUCATION CONCEPT Professional military education is the term used to distinguish between the broad-liberal education provided by societal higher education institutions and that education which is provided and focused on the military

[3941] The efficacy of professional military education depends to a large extent on the quality of the initial broad-liberal education provided as a foundation

[3942] Professional military education is provided by the military in conjunction with or independently of tertiary institutions of higher learning and is directed towards specific military professional and occupational specific knowledge

[3943] The spectrum of knowledge that is addressed during this education is applicable to all aspects and spheres of the profession of arms

[3944] MILITARY TRAINING CONCEPT Military training is rooted in the need for action

[3945] It places the focus on the primary operational functions of the military and the skills required to do that well

[3946] Training is thus directed towards instilling the necessary technical and tactical military skills to perform effectively

[3947] Training is mostly a group-oriented activity to instil armed forces with an ability ‘to do’

[3948] Training constitutes the foundation of an appropriate military culture and is largely a closed process for the translation of doctrine into action, inculcation of discipline, and establishment of cohesion

[3949] Good training produces military personnel who respond instinctively to anticipated, recognisable circumstances in a manner circumscribed by the doctrine and culture to which they have been trained

[3950] FOUNDATIONAL MILITARY EDUCATION AND TRAINING CONCEPT Foundational education and training refers to the initial orientation, training, and education of the officer recruits of the Defence Force

[3951] It defines the process through which officer recruits are inducted into the Defence Force and inculcated with the appropriate skills, knowledge and attitudes needed for a career as a military professional

[3952] The future military leader (officers and other ranks) requires a balance between thinking and fighting

[3953] This foundational military development will be rooted in an understanding of the uniqueness of the military profession and will be done by the individual Services

[3954] The officer career path will in general be rooted in quality tertiary-level broad-liberal education and professional military training

[3955] The WO and NCO career path will be rooted in professional military training, supported by exposure to a wide range of military experiences, to ensure a skills and mentor-driven approach to leadership by WOs and NCOs

[3956] Though a tertiary-level education is not a prerequisite for WOs and NCOs, it is nonetheless encouraged

[3957] FUNCTIONAL MILITARY DEVELOPMENT CONCEPT

[3958] This development also relates to the immediate working environment and is normally of an immediate applied practical and functional nature

[3959] Development thus relates to learning activities that occur outside the formal career-related education and training programmes of the Defence Force

[3960] RECRUITMENT CONCEPT Recruitment programmes are rooted in the enhanced status of the Defence Force in society

[3961] The military is a practical profession that balances military adventure with excellent military education and learning opportunities

[3962] It is this combination of experiences that attracts young men and women to the Defence Force

[3963] Defence recruitment importantly pursues diversified recruitment opportunities throughout society, ranging from geographical recruitment at the grass-roots level to the targeted recruitment of its future leaders

[3964] The recruitment of future defence leaders will occur in a very competitive labour market

[3965] Recruitment is broadly representative of the people of South Africa, with due consideration being given to matters of equity

[3966] The Defence Force must have a dedicated decentralised officer recruitment programme based on the deliberate selection of individuals from schools and universities with demonstrable leadership qualities and who meet the academic and professional profile required of the future military leader

[3967] Recruitment of other ranks is broad-based and spread throughout South Africa to ensure that the breadth of South African society is represented in a provincially proportionate manner

[3968] A balance is ensured between the urban and rural backgrounds of enlisted recruits

[3969] LEADERSHIP CONCEPT All education and training of rank-bearing personnel will be directed towards the development of leadership attributes and qualities and is steered towards a culture of decisive, timeous decision-making

[3970] The defence doctrinal tenet of mission command will be instilled

[3971] Education, training and development will be based on an understanding of the difference between and the need for both

[3973] LIFE-LONG LEARNING CONCEPT Career progression in the Defence Force will be linked to the concept of life-long learning

[3974] Members will be encouraged to take personal responsibility for their own learning experiences and career development activities

[3975] ACCREDITED LEARNING CONCEPT

[3976] All learning in the career path of officers, WOs and NCOs will be accredited within the NQF and adhere to the requirements of the South African Qualifications Authority (SAQA

[3977] The Defence Force will, as far as possible, partner its military professional education with existing programmes at universities and other institutions of higher learning and ensure accreditation of its own training programmes

[3979] foundational officer military education and training will be delivered through a single, tailored military institution which is linked to an established national tertiary institution

[3980] From a top-down perspective, the advanced education and training of officers, WOs and NCOs will be pursued through access to a variety of institutions of higher learning, both domestically and internationally

[3982] Cooperation and support, however, are required from institutions of higher learning for the education of military personnel

[3983] The Defence Force will thus ensure an appropriate balance between an in-house training capacity and the out-sourcing of education to institutions of higher learning

[3984] Partnerships will be established with recognised institutions of higher learning for both quality education and training in the Defence Force

[3985] Foundational education, training and development is directed towards military professionalism and the preparation of military personnel for a career in the armed forces

[3986] Joint and service-unique requirements will be balanced in the education, training and development of military personnel

[3987] The officer cadet phase follows foundational military training at the Services

[3988] EDUCATION, TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT LINKED TO DEFENCE DOCTRINE The interplay between military education, training, development and military operations is of critical importance for the strategic positioning of the Defence Force and the professionalism of its members

[3989] The Defence Force will thus link its education, training and development programmes with the doctrine domain

[3990] The military operations domain executes successful military operations through the application of military doctrine in each mission and collates new experience for integration into existing doctrine or the development of new doctrine

[3991] The education domain integrates broad security, strategic and military considerations with the experience derived by defence members in operations so that adjustment to and development of doctrine can occur

[3992] The training domain develops suitable training regimes and inculcates soldiers with the appropriate functional and war-fighting skills

[3993] The training domain must be responsive to and able to adapt to new doctrinal realities

[3994] The interplay between these domains will be coordinated by the operations, doctrine and training staffs of the Chief of the Defence Force

[3995] The Defence Force is recognised as a key institution for the development of leadership within the wider South African society

[3996] There will be no compromise on the education, training and development of the future officer; to do so would have dire implications for the operational success of the Defence Force

[3999] The Officer Corps is the collective commissioned leadership of the Defence Force

[4001] The Officer Corps must have a comprehensive and sound education, comprehensive and current training and the experience to enable it to meet new challenges effectively as they arise and evolve

[4006] Specialist and professional candidate officers specifically recruited to pursue professional or specialist academic programmes at contracted tertiary institutions, and who will receive foundational military training from the Services, including an academic preparation programme prior to commencing studies

[4010] Late-entry candidate officers from the NCO and WO ranks who are functional or technical specialists, and who are identified for officer appointment

[4052] PROFESSIONAL SKILLS REQUIRED OF THE WO AND NCO CORPS

[4053] The value of the WO and NCO arises from the experience built up over many years of service

[4054] WOs and senior NCOs have more experience than most junior officers with whom they will work

[4055] Senior NCO skills are developed over time and are founded in practical application

[4057] The technical specialists of the WO and NCO Corps carry the responsibility for ensuring that the assigned equipment is properly maintained and serviceable for use when required, while the administrative specialists carry the responsibility for the effective and efficient running of the unit, and particularly for ensuring that the personnel, logistic and financial systems are implemented correctly and function effectively

[4058] The combat WO and NCO Corps are in many respects the military craftsmen, skilled in the craft of individual and small-group combat tactics, in leadership and in the combat aspects of the particular branch of the Service

[4064] A sound grasp of battle drills, and the ability to execute them under conditions of extreme stress

[4125] DEFENCE EDUCATION AND TRAINING APPROACH THE DEFENCE EDUCATION AND TRAINING PHILOSOPHY

[4126] The following underpinning defence education and training philosophy provides a holistic approach for military professional education and training, starting from foundational education and training and progressing up to the level of advanced national security studies

[4127] Due cognisance is given to the alignment of Defence Force operational requirements with corresponding academic qualification levels

[4128] This holistic approach honours the ‘one-force’ concept and provides education, training and development systems for the Regulars, Reserves and defence civilians

[4129] An auxiliary service will have its own specific education, training and development requirements

[4130] The defence training system is structured to deliver within the broad milestones reflected below and is provided by the following organisational groupings and capabilities

[4131] FOUNDATIONAL MILITARY EDUCATION AND TRAINING Services will provide foundational military training for all soldiers

[4132] The Defence Academy, as the officer commissioning authority, will provide the foundational education to officer cadets and candidate officers to enable their commissioning as junior officers in the Defence Force

[4133] PROFESSIONAL MILITARY EDUCATION AND TRAINING Services, as the military competency authorities, provide the colleges and schools that deliver the following accredited programmes: a. Formative Non-Commissioned Training

[4134] Formative training, which includes induction training and current basic military training, must be presented by the Services to inculcate both the common/joint military culture and the Service-specific culture

[4135] Period from entry to WO

[4136] b. Services Junior Training and Functional Training

[4137] This training is the responsibility of the Services (as military competency authorities) as well as Services and Divisions (as functional competency authorities) and is structured to render deployable soldiers

[4138] The focus is on providing appropriate professional military education and training

[4139] Period from lieutenant/corporal to captain/staff sergeant.) c. Joint Warfare Training

[4140] The principle of joint warfare and battle handling training at all levels is emphasised

[4141] To this end, joint warfare training will be presented at both the junior officer and senior officer level and from the NCO up to senior WO level

[4142] At the junior levels, the principles of joint warfare will be taught in order to prepare the defence member for joint higher warfare training

[4143] d. Services Senior Command & Staff and Functional Training

[4144] This training is the responsibility of the Services and must provide sufficient professional military education and training for entry into senior service and the joint, interagency, interdepartmental and multinational operational environment

[4145] Period from majors/WOs to lieutenant colonels

[4146] e. Force Training

[4147] This training is the responsibility of the Services and provides combat-ready capabilities

[4148] The Operations Headquarters, at the operational level, will provide mission-ready training for the application of combat-ready capabilities at the different levels of operational and tactical deployments

[4149] FUNCTION-ORIENTED EDUCATION AND TRAINING Services and Divisions, as the functional competency authorities, provide and/or coordinate accredited function-oriented education and training as follows: a. Functional Training and Academic Integration

[4188] A Defence Academy must be established to provide foundational education, training and development to all officers of the Defence Force

[4191] a. Officer Cadet Programme

[4203] BASIC TENETS OF THE DEFENCE ACADEMY The Defence Academy must be, at all times, a symbol of military professionalism and leadership excellence, and a reflection of civil-military relations in South Africa

[4204] Education, training and development is presented in a complementary manner that ensures appropriate levels of knowledge and skills as well as the development of an appropriate military ethos

[4205] The focus of the education, training and development programmes at the Defence Academy must be on the enhancement of leadership potential and a military culture that enhances the professional ethos of the Defence Force

[4206] The Services are responsible for foundational military training prior to entry to the Defence Academy, further military training during the four-year programme, and Service-specific training during the last six months at the Defence Academy

[4207] This training prepares members for appointment to their respective Services

[4210] The recognition of the military as the training authority and the university as the education authority
